subject: design/solution-shape-v1
statement: A shape is `authoritative` from its design's approval until the code implementing it exists; then its status becomes `superseded-by-code` and the code is the source of truth (FR-5). While `authoritative` and pre-code, a shape-confined change is a **re-approval** of the shape — the design is untouched (DINV-5); this is legal because the shape is non-frozen. A change that would alter the design's binding markup is not a shape change at all — it is a Decision change and takes the design's supersession path (DINV-5, FR-6). How "the implementing code exists" is signalled to flip the status is an open question (§7 Q2); until resolved, the flip is an explicit authoring act recorded in the shape header. A `superseded-by-code` shape is retained as a dated record but drops out of "the authoritative shape" resolution; the code answers "what is the shape now."
